label: miso 63 shortout rpe
definition: miso-63 composed candidate (main) -- miso-62 keeper meta.json replay + miso_rpe_pricing (the miso-61 published $200 RPE demand value on the RDT violation tiers) + unit_outage_short_windows (< 5-day baseload-coal CEMS windows, the July-2025 availability layer; docs/DIAGNOSIS-miso-july2025-lmp-2026-07.md). Zero fitted parameters added; both mechanisms separately evidenced (miso-61 registered run; _miso_shortout_probe 2025 A/B).
market_story: Two real-market layers composed onto the miso-62 keeper, both zero fitted parameters. (1) RPE violation pricing (miso-61): MISO enforces subregional short-term-reserve requirements by RPE constraints over the RDT, and in the 2023-2025 design the published $200/MWh RPE demand value applies ADDITIVELY with the RDT TCDC in real violations — so Midwest-South separation in violation hours prices $240/$700, not $40/$500. (2) Short forced outages (< 5 days) of baseload coal, measured per-unit in CEMS, which the standard 5-day outage floor makes invisible — they concentrate exactly in stressed periods (Cayuga 531 MW and Belle River 700 MW were offline AT the Jul 28-29 2025 heat-event peak), so the model otherwise carries phantom peak capacity. Result: every scored 2025 price/volume metric moves toward actual (C3a -16.5% -> -15.9%, C3b 0.212 -> 0.206; the v2.5-diagnostic C2 rows: gas -6.8% -> -6.1%, coal-over +4.0% -> +3.1%), 2024 gets MISO's first 4 DA tail hours >$200, and C1 holds at its best (14/16 all, 10/12 free).
